summary: In the Capernaum synagogue, Jesus tells the crowd He fed that He Himself is the bread of life, and many disciples turn away while the Twelve stay.
key_insight: Jesus told the crowd, “you seek Me, not because you saw the signs, but because you ate of the loaves.” They had eaten the miracle without reading the sign. The bread was meant to point to Him, and when He offered Himself instead of more bread, many walked away.
story: The next day, the crowd on the far shore realized that Jesus had not left with His disciples, yet He was gone. Boats came over from Tiberias, so they crossed to Capernaum looking for Him. When they found Him, they asked, “Rabbi, when did You come here?”

Jesus answered, “Most assuredly, I say to you, you seek Me, not because you saw the signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.” He told them, “Do not labor for the food which perishes, but for the food which endures to everlasting life.” When they asked what works God required, He said, “This is the work of God, that you believe in Him whom He sent.”

They asked for a sign. “Our fathers ate the manna in the desert,” they said. Jesus answered that Moses had not given them the bread from heaven, “but My Father gives you the true bread from heaven.” They said, “Lord, give us this bread always.” Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. He who comes to Me shall never hunger, and he who believes in Me shall never thirst.” All that the Father gives Him will come to Him, “and the one who comes to Me I will by no means cast out.” He would lose none of them, but raise them up at the last day.

The Jews began to complain: “Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?” Jesus told them to stop murmuring. “No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him.” Their fathers ate manna in the wilderness and died, but He said, “I am the living bread which came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever; and the bread that I shall give is My flesh, which I shall give for the life of the world.”

They argued among themselves, “How can this Man give us His flesh to eat?” Jesus went further: “Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you have no life in you.” Whoever feeds on Him abides in Him and will live forever. He said these things in the synagogue as He taught in Capernaum.

Many of His disciples said, “This is a hard saying; who can understand it?” Jesus asked them, “Does this offend you? What then if you should see the Son of Man ascend where He was before? It is the Spirit who gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and they are life.” From that time many of His disciples went back and walked with Him no more.

Jesus turned to the Twelve: “Do you also want to go away?” Simon Peter answered, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. Also we have come to believe and know that You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Jesus answered, “Did I not choose you, the twelve, and one of you is a devil?” He meant Judas Iscariot, who would betray Him.

scene.label: Manna again
scene.text: The crowd quoted Scripture, “He gave them bread from heaven to eat” (see Psalm 78:24; Exodus 16:4). Some Jewish writings from the late first century hoped that manna would fall again in the days of the Messiah (2 Baruch 29:8). After yesterday’s bread, the crowd wanted a Moses who would feed them every day.

scene.label: The synagogue at Capernaum
scene.text: The white limestone synagogue visitors see in Capernaum today was built centuries later. Beneath it lie the black basalt foundations of an earlier synagogue, probably the one where Jesus taught these words.

scene.label: Murmuring
scene.text: John says the Jews “complained” and Jesus told them, “Do not murmur.” It is the same complaint Israel made in the wilderness, right before God sent the manna (Exodus 16:2–4).

scene.label: Flesh and blood
scene.text: The Law forbade eating any blood (Leviticus 17:10–14), so Jesus’ words shocked His hearers. Christians differ on whether He speaks here of the Lord’s Supper. Many read eating and drinking as a vivid picture of believing (compare 6:47 with 6:54); others see the Supper in view, at least indirectly. All agree He points to His death “for the life of the world.”

witnesses.john: Only John records this teaching. He sets it the day after the feeding, so the sign is followed by its meaning, as often in his Gospel. It is the first of Jesus’ seven “I am” sayings with a picture, and it ends with the first great sifting of His followers and Peter’s confession on behalf of the Twelve.

seeing.reveals: Jesus does not merely give bread; He is the bread. He offers Himself, given in death “for the life of the world,” and promises to keep and raise up everyone the Father gives Him.
seeing.living: Many followed Jesus while He fed them and left when He offered Himself. Come to Him for Himself, not only for what He provides. When His words are hard, answer as Peter did: “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.”
seeing.ponder: Are you seeking Jesus for the loaves, or for Himself?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus does not just give bread; He is the bread, and only He satisfies.
outline: The bread that must be received (41–58)
preaching.watch_for: The audience narrows as the teaching deepens: the crowd (6:24), “the Jews” (6:41), many disciples (6:60), and finally the Twelve (6:67). Each group meets a harder word and must decide.
